analysis.hypothesis: The model requires two custom CUDA kernels: softmax over dimension 1 (after dividing by temperature) and element-wise square. Both must handle non-contiguous tensors via strides, and softmax must be numerically stable. Implementing these as grid-stride kernels will satisfy the contract and likely outperform torch.compile.
evidence: model_new.py calls cuda_extension.softmax_dim1(x, self.temperature) and cuda_extension.mul_square(x).
custom_ops_contract.json specifies softmax_dim1(x: Tensor float32 cuda [N,C,H,W], temperature: double) -> Tensor same shape/dtype/device; mul_square(x: Tensor) -> Tensor.
The reference does softmax along dim=1 on x/0.5; tensor is 4D [16,1024,32,32] with strides [1048576,1024,32,1] (contiguous).
Numerical stability requires subtracting per-slice max before exp.
No conv/convtranspose, so only raw CUDA kernels needed.
changes: Implement softmax_dim1_launcher: float32 kernel computing max over dim=1 using strides, then exp(x/temperature - max) and sum, then normalizing.
Implement mul_square_launcher: element-wise square using strides.
Use grid-stride loops to handle large sizes and comply with grid caps.
Provide extern "C" launchers with cudaStream_t parameter for binding.
Check for CUDA errors after launch.
